newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RMB takes breather after recent run.
newsitem.headline: RMB takes breather after recent run.

text.p: Shares in South African financial services and banking group RMB Holdings were heavily traded on Tuesday, first rising to a fresh recent high and then edging back on profit-taking, dealers said.
By 1315 GMT over 2.74 million RMB shares had changed hands, making it the third most actively traded stock on the market.
Dealers said the stock had seen a number of bookovers, where buyers and sellers are matched by the same brokerage.
Shares were last trading at 13.45 rand, off 20 cents from its previous close, after earlier rising to 13.70.
"It's had a good run in the past few days. It moved up this morning on not too much volume, but now sellers are starting to see value at this price," a dealer said.
RMB has powered up almost 27 percent since the beginning of the month, in tandem with other banking stocks which have pushed the bank-laden financial index to several new record highs.

Financial stocks have recently feasted on a brighter outlook for a cut in interest rates following a batch of data indicating that the economy is cooling off. A raft of merger activity in the sector and the fact that the index underperformed last year were also seen as other positives.

Other bullish factors for RMB include an announcement last week that it planned to invest 500 million rand over five years to create a new merchant banking division which would be more customer focused.
